facts.statement: Holdenius is a monospecific genus containing only one species.
Holdenius was previously classified in the family Dunkleosteidae but is now placed in the family Aspinothoracidi.
facts.quote: Previously classified as belonging to the family Dunkleosteidae, it is now considered to be a member of Aspinothoracidi, the sister clade to Dunkleosteoidea.

facts.statement: Holdenius was a large arthrodire fish that grew to a length of about 3 meters.
facts.quote: Holdenius was a large arthrodire, reaching lengths of around 3 m.

facts.statement: Holdenius was a piscivore that used sharp shearing plates in its jaws to cut prey into pieces.
facts.quote: Holdenius was a piscivorous animal that used its sharp shearing gnathal plates to seize and cleave its prey into manageable pieces.

facts.statement: A fossil specimen of Holdenius was found preserved next to a Ctenacanth fish that had been bitten in half.
facts.quote: One articulated specimen of this placoderm from the Upper Devonian Cleveland Shale was preserved adjacent to the remains of its prey; a Ctenacanth chondrichthyan, which had been bitten in half.

facts.statement: Because its prey was over half its size, Holdenius is inferred to have been an exceptionally aggressive predator.
facts.quote: Considering its prey was over half its size, it can be inferred that Holdenius was an exceptionally aggressive nektonic predator.

facts.statement: A spine from a prey fish was found lodged in the braincase of a Holdenius specimen, likely causing instant death.
facts.quote: An anterior dorsal spine from the ctenacanth was found lodged in the palate and extending into the braincase of the Holdenius, likely killing it instantly.

facts.statement: Holdenius lived during the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Holdenius is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish which lived during the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Holdenius lived between 365.2 and 358.86 million years ago during the Famennian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (365.2 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Holdenius was described by Dunkle and Bungart in 1942.
The Spanish taxonomic record lists Holdenius as belonging to the family Dunkleosteidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Holdenius as Dinichthyidae.

rejected.statement: Holdenius is known only from isolated jaw bones and is morphologically similar to the genus Dunkleosteus.
rejected.quote: This placoderm is known only from isolated jaw bones, and little is known about it except that it is relatively morphologically similar to its more famous relative Dunkleosteus.
